chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'What do you think of one who arrives in a town? Until when should he shorten the prayer, and when should he complete it?' He said, 'When you enter a land and are certain that you will stay there for ten days, complete the prayer. And if you do not know how long your stay will be, saying

key_terms.شَهْرٌ: A month (duration after which completion is required)

ai.seo_question: When should a traveler shorten their prayers versus completing them according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between a traveler (musafir) and a resident (muqim) based on the duration of stay, establishing ten days as the threshold for completing prayers. It introduces the concept of 'uncertain stay' (shakk al-maqam), allowing the traveler to maintain the status of a traveler and shorten prayers until a full month elapses, even if they depart immediately after the month completes. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining prayer length during extended travel or temporary residence in a new locale.
